(Nasdaq: DPZ), the largest pizza company in the world, announced results for the third quarter of 2026. “As I step into the CEO role, I am honored to lead Domino’s and build on the competitive advantages that have long set us apart: our iconic brand, best-in-class franchise system, global scale and proven operating capabilities,” said Joe Jordan, Domino’s Chief Executive Officer. “Our opportunity now is to capitalize on those strengths by getting even closer to our customers, helping our franchisees grow their profitability and turning our best performance into our everyday performance. By advancing winning ideas faster and executing them with greater clarity, speed and consistency, we can earn more occasions, continue gaining market share and create meaningful long-term value for shareholders. Domino’s has always been at its best when we are a step ahead. That mindset has helped us set the pace for the industry before, and it’s how we’ll push ourselves to do it again. I believe our next chapter will be our strongest yet.” Third Quarter of 2026 Operational and Financial Highlights (Unaudited): The tables below outline certain statistical measures utilized by the Company to analyze its performance, as well as key financial results. This historical data is not necessarily indicative of results to be expected for any future period. Revenues increased $38.5 million, or 3.4%, in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to higher supply chain revenues and higher global franchise royalty revenues. The increase in supply chain revenues was primarily attributable to higher order volumes, as well as an increase in the Company’s food basket pricing to stores, which increased 2.2% in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025. U.S. and international franchise royalties and fees revenues increased primarily as a result of net store growth during the trailing four quarters. These increases in revenues were partially offset by lower U.S. Company-owned store revenues as a result of the refranchising of certain U.S. Company-owned store markets in the second quarter of 2026. • Supply chain gross margin increased 0.9 percentage points in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to procurement productivity. • Income from operations increased $18.6 million, or 8.3%, in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025. Excluding the negative impact of foreign currency exchange rates on international franchise royalty revenues of $0.2 million, income from operations increased $18.8 million, or 8.4%, primarily due to the increases in U.S. and international franchise royalties and fees revenues and gross margin dollar growth within supply chain. • Net income increased $12.9 million, or 9.2%, in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to higher income from operations. • Diluted EPS was $4.60 in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to $4.08 in the third quarter of 2025, representing a $0.52, or 12.7%, increase. The increase in diluted EPS was driven by higher net income, as well as a lower weighted average diluted share count resulting from the Company’s share repurchases during the trailing four quarters. • Net cash provided by operating activities was $520.6 million in the three fiscal quarters of 2026 as compared to $552.3 million in the three fiscal quarters of 2025. The Company spent $60.8 million on capital expenditures in the three fiscal quarters of 2026 as compared to $56.7 million in the three fiscal quarters of 2025, resulting in free cash flow of $459.8 million in the three fiscal quarters of 2026 as compared to $495.6 million in the three fiscal quarters of 2025. The decrease in free cash flow was a result of the timing and amount of payments for advertising activities and the negative impact of changes in operating assets and liabilities. These decreases were partially offset by the increase in income from operations in the three fiscal quarters of 2026 (excluding the pre-tax realized gain on the sale of the Company’s fully depreciated corporate aircraft in the first quarter of 2026). Quarterly Dividend Subsequent to the end of the third quarter of 2026, on October 6, 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors declared a $1.99 per share quarterly dividend on its outstanding common stock for shareholders of record as of December 15, 2026, to be paid on December 30, 2026. Share Repurchases During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased and retired 216,282 shares of common stock for a total of $73.6 million. During the three fiscal quarters of 2026, the Company repurchased and retired 848,503 shares of common stock for a total of $304.9 million. As of September 6, 2026, the Company had a total remaining authorized amount for share repurchases of $1.15 billion. Comments on Regulation G In addition to the GAAP financial measures set forth in this press release, the Company has included non-GAAP financial measures within the meaning of Regulation G, including free cash flow, income from operations, excluding foreign currency impact and Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA. The Company has also included metrics such as global retail sales, global retail sales growth (excluding foreign currency impact), same store sales growth, net store growth, food basket pricing change, impact of changes in foreign currency exchange rates on international franchise royalty revenues and the leverage ratio, which are commonly used statistical measures in the quick-service restaurant industry that are important to understanding Company performance. The Company uses “global retail sales,” a statistical measure, to refer to total worldwide retail sales at Company-owned and franchised stores. The Company believes global retail sales information is useful in analyzing revenues because franchisees pay royalties and, in the U.S., advertising fees that are based on a percentage of franchise retail sales. The Company reviews comparable industry global retail sales information to assess business trends and to track the growth of the Domino’s Pizza brand, and believes it is indicative of the financial health of the Company’s franchisee base. In addition, supply chain revenues are directly impacted by changes in franchise retail sales in the U.S. and Canada. As a result, sales by Domino’s franchisees have a direct effect on the Company’s profitability. Retail sales for franchised stores are reported to the Company by its franchisees and are not included in Company revenues. “Global retail sales growth” is calculated as the change of U.S. Dollar global retail sales against the comparable period of the prior year. “Global retail sales growth, excluding foreign currency impact,” is calculated as the change of local currency global retail sales against the comparable period of the prior year. Changes in global retail sales growth, excluding foreign currency impact are primarily driven by same store sales growth and net store growth. The Company uses “same store sales growth,” a statistical measure, which is calculated for a given period by including only sales from stores that also had sales in the comparable weeks of both periods. International same store sales growth is calculated similarly to U.S. same store sales growth. Changes in international same store sales are reported on a constant dollar basis, which reflects changes in international local currency sales. Same store sales growth for transferred stores is reflected in their current classification. The Company uses “net store growth,” a statistical measure, which is calculated by netting gross store openings with gross store closures during the period. Transfers between Company-owned stores and franchised stores are excluded from the calculation of net store growth. The Company uses “food basket pricing change,” a statistical measure, which is calculated as the percentage change of the food basket (including both food and cardboard products) purchased by an average U.S. store (based on average weekly unit sales) from U.S. supply chain centers against the comparable period of the prior year. The Company believes that the food basket pricing change is important to understanding Company performance because as food basket prices fluctuate, revenues, cost of sales and gross margin percentages in the Company’s supply chain segment also fluctuate. Additionally, cost of sales, gross margins and gross margin percentages for the Company’s U.S. Company-owned stores also fluctuate. The Company uses “free cash flow,” which is calculated as net cash provided by operating activities, less capital expenditures, both as reported under GAAP. The most directly comparable financial measure calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP is net cash provided by operating activities. reference.summary: Domino's Pizza, Inc. operates as a pizza company worldwide. The company operates through three segments: U.S. Stores, International Franchise, and Supply Chain. It offers pizzas under the Domino's brand name through company-owned and franchised stores. The company also provides bread products, wings, boneless chicken, pastas, oven-baked sandwiches, soft drink products and desserts. In addition, it offers parmesan stuffed crust pizza; spicy chicken bacon ranch specialty pizza; and garlic, and cinnamon bread bites, as well as croissant, chocolate volcano, and chicken burst pizzas. Domino's Pizza, Inc. was founded in 1960 and is based in Ann Arbor, Michigan.
